scope.role: Choosing and reviewing small enterprise structural patterns and their contracts.
criteria: Verify actual caller semantics before choosing base patterns; preserve no-change and simpler alternatives.
Keep identity, state, lifetime, concurrency and representation guarantees distinct from pattern names.
For already-included Value Object guidance, separate generated record equality, ownership and the domain's equality/representation policy.
Keep established gateway outcomes, stub scope, plugin authority and pattern handoffs without broadening into neighboring skills.
scope.instructions: Read wave4 brief, complete review prompt, root AGENTS, parallel review workflow and skill-engineering with evidence/evaluation/resource-design/anti-pattern references. Reused unchanged prior comparative research and inspected wave4 lessons/roadmap portions. No nested owned AGENTS found.

baseline.scopedGitStatus: Clean at assignment; no staged, unstaged or untracked owned files.

findingsCorrected.severity: Consequential missing precondition, not an observed production defect
findingsCorrected.originalGuidance: Records were summarized as giving equality and shallow immutability, with defensive ownership required for mutable components.
findingsCorrected.gap: That can conflate ownership with suitable Value Object equality. Array components use identity; defensive copies alone can leave unequal independently constructed values and violate the record reconstruction invariant.
findingsCorrected.implemented: Qualify component-derived equality; require the caller's equivalence contract, coherent equals/hashCode or an appropriate immutable representation; identify independent equal keys, reconstruction, lookup and mutation checks.
findingsCorrected.consequence: Avoids silently ineffective value-based cache/stub keys and ownership-only fixes that still break record contracts.
evidence: 24 focused local assertions and expected failing wrong-array-fix control

findingsCorrected.gap: Generated component equality may differ from numerical equivalence, while an indiscriminate normalization can erase valid representation semantics.
findingsCorrected.implemented: State BigDecimal value-plus-scale equality versus numerical comparison; normalize only under the accepted domain contract and inspect consumers/serialization before changing representation.
findingsCorrected.consequence: Allows numeric-equivalence keys when justified and preserves distinct precision-bearing values when required; a mapper must not silently choose this business policy.
evidence: Java 17 BigDecimal equals/compareTo/hashCode and representation contracts
Local checks and expected failing wrong-decimal-normalization control
Paired development fixtures differing only in accepted scale significance

filesChangedByReviewer.reason: Focused Value Object decision guard and version-matched primary-source links; all existing examples retained.
Patch bump required for content changes.

preservedCapabilities: All eight main patterns and their scope, concrete triggers, simpler alternatives and conditional handoffs.
Gateway vocabulary/error translation, unknown external effects, retry/transaction cautions and controllable time/identity/storage seams.
Input-sensitive Service Stub behavior, stable keys, instance ownership, missing setup rejection and explicit lack of thread safety/transport coverage.
Layer Supertype cohesion, JPA transient/persisted/detached/proxied identity caveats and lack of automatic equality guarantees.
Separated Interface dependency direction and compatibility/wiring limits.
Registry scope, tenant selection, compound operations, missing entries and cleanup ownership.
Special Case agreed domain operations, presentation distinctions, absence versus failure/authorization semantics.
Plugin configuration/extension justification, per-tenant selection, provider creation and trusted-versus-untrusted execution boundary.
Record Set/CachedRowSet support and bounded tabular representation choices.
Existing TaxId narrow-format illustration and explicit lack of check-digit/jurisdiction/ownership validation.

versions.rationale: Single patch for changed immutable package contents; no prior uncommitted bump. Shared index remains coordinator-owned.

executed.detail: Repository package loader/validator reports four files, version 1.2.6, zero issues and two valid local links; scoped Prettier and git diff --check passed.

24 assertions cover default array identity, constructor/accessor ownership, copy-only record failure, coherent content equality/hashing/lookup/reconstruction, numeric versus scale-sensitive decimal identity, and representation changes.
wrong-array-fix and wrong-decimal-normalization each exit 1 with the targeted AssertionError. These are intentionally incorrect hypotheses rejected by the checks.

Compiled four shared fixture sources --release17 and ran Demo. Observed empty lookup for a different-scale key, two cache entries and reports 2.0 kg / 2.00 kg. This observation is interpreted differently under the two accepted contracts.
12 consistency checks prove all seven ordinary task/source files are byte-identical and only the accepted scale-significance paragraph differs.

Owner: measurement API maintainer. Status: accepted. All calls in this fixture are sequential and the cache belongs to this module instance. files.requirements.md:
# Accepted client contract

Owner: measurement API maintainer. Status: accepted. All calls in this fixture are sequential and the cache belongs to this module instance. Quantities must remain exact decimal values with their units; do not convert them through binary floating point. Null amount/unit is invalid. Different units identify different measurements. Cache identity and reports must follow the measurement meaning below.

The submitted decimal scale records measurement precision and is part of its identity. Equal magnitudes reported at different precision must remain distinct measurements, and reports preserve that submitted scale.

expectedOutcome: Read requirements and the cache/formatter, rather than approving from record syntax or naming alone.
Explain the existing cache distinction for equal numeric values of different scale and the formatting implications.
Support numeric-equivalence normalization under this explicit contract or a compatible explicit equality/representation design, with exact decimal arithmetic and units preserved.
Correct the proposal's assertion that callers are unaffected: formatter output changes intentionally toward the accepted canonical representation.
Propose or execute checks for equal numeric keys/hashes/reconstruction, different quantities and units, and report serialization; do not treat raw record generation as domain policy.
failureConditions: Rejects all normalization merely because BigDecimal equals includes scale despite the accepted numeric-only contract.
Claims normalization never changes consumer output.
Uses double conversion, rounds meaningful digits, collapses units or invents a new mandatory pattern/framework.
Claims a run or measured behavioral improvement without execution evidence.

expectedOutcome: Treat accepted scale significance as the decisive changed constraint.
Reject unconditional constructor normalization and retain the current scale-sensitive equality/cache separation and report representation unless a separate approved purpose requires a separate type.
Update the proposed disposition and rationale, using cache and formatter evidence; do not leave a refuted recommendation as the final decision.
Verify or propose checks preserving distinct precision keys and report strings, while same numeric value plus same scale/unit remains equal.
Keep unrelated null/unit invariants and scoped sequential cache intact.
failureConditions: Normalizes or numerically compares measurement identity, merging distinct accepted precision values.
Changes only the report formatting while cache equality still merges required identities.
Adds a mapper to conceal or redefine the accepted representation policy.
Reports a generic warning but approves the refuted proposal.
